concept: Config server placement and cost (dedicated vs embedded)
summary: Source-anchored research for Config server placement and cost (dedicated vs embedded). Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Current Atlas HTML docs select embedded config servers for ten or fewer shards and dedicated config servers above ten when Atlas management is enabled. Shard-count changes trigger reselection; upgrading 7.0 to 8.0 enables management without immediately changing the existing type. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Embedded-to-dedicated conversion drains user data and adds a replacement shard to retain the target shard count. Atlas describes an online process that can take hours to days for large datasets, increases receiving-shard resource use and prevents concurrent tier/storage changes; provision headroom first. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Percona's June 26, 2025 engineering article argues that config shards reduce overhead for small clusters, but favors separate roles for large clusters because their relative infrastructure saving is small. This is qualitative advice, not a measured Atlas savings percentage. (low confidence)

Disabling Atlas-managed config servers selects dedicated placement and immediately starts conversion for an eligible embedded cluster; it is a topology and capacity change, rather than merely an administrative preference. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Embedded config servers colocate application data and cluster metadata; dedicated config servers use a separate metadata replica set. Embedded placement reduces infrastructure overhead, especially for smaller clusters. (high confidence)

Atlas documents a three-node M30 replica set for dedicated config servers; its transition procedure scales the former config shard down to M30 after user data drains. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers.md

For dedicated config servers, Atlas bills config nodes at a separate rate included in cluster cost; selected application tier and storage do not determine that rate. Do not estimate this overhead by multiplying the application-node rate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Global Clusters do not support embedded config servers. Replica-set-to-sharded conversion produces dedicated config servers even with Atlas management enabled; Search and certain unsharded encrypted or time-series collections can block automatic transitions. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/transition-to-dedicated-config-servers.md

In Atlas 8.0+, replica set IDs containing 'config' can hold application data and IDs containing 'shard' can hold either or both data roles. Avoid assigning infrastructure cost roles solely from those name fragments. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Atlas does not document a showback or tag taxonomy for config server placement. Documented facts relevant to showback: embedded config server clusters cost less than dedicated ones, Atlas-managed config servers re-select the config server type automatically when shards are added or removed, and some clusters (replica set conversions, Global Clusters, Search users) stay dedicated or pinned regardless of the management setting. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-additional-settings.md

Canonical's Charmed MongoDB guide treats config-server and shard applications as separately scalable replica sets and requires draining before removing a shard application. This independently documents deployment-role separation, but does not establish Atlas billing or embedded-placement policy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-23)
